Make only these corrections:
1. In TOP-RIGHT and BOTTOM-RIGHT cells, the full entrance-wall foil/fabric screen must cover the small left window too, with uninterrupted plain crinkled foil there. Preserve the sink and existing vent access. Its top edge is tied directly to original fabric seam tabs with simple short soft ties. Remove any appearance of a rigid rail, metal rings or hard brackets: show a gently sagging plain fabric upper edge BETWEEN the existing tabs, no straight metal rod.
2. In BOTTOM-LEFT and BOTTOM-RIGHT cells, reveal a narrow clearly visible strip of the light GREY SYNTHETIC CARGO NET underneath the cloth canopy along its front edge, and a small exposed triangle at one corner. This is the supporting net that holds the canopy ABOVE the tallest foliage, with ventilation. It is a flexible square knotted fibre grid matching the centre soybean support, held in tension by thin cords tied directly to the existing wall seam tabs. The beige cloth is folded back just enough at that front edge to reveal the net, without changing the canopy's main shape or adding a rigid front bar. Keep the large front air gap, soft side drapes and two small plain roll-up ties. Do not add vertical poles, frames, rods, extra lamps, timber or buckles.
3. In ALL cells, the top edges of the three brick beds are only thin folded cream waterproof sheet, matching the austere planting/tending family. Replace the thick dark rounded padded-looking edging with thin creased sheet draped over the existing same brick rim; do not change wall height, footprint, plant height or the plain loose potato surface cover.
No new decorative details, no labels, no borders. Exactly the same scene with only those material corrections.
